messages:
maya: quick heads-up — canary for hosted inference showed a ~12% p50 regression on streaming endpoints after the 03:00 deploy. cpu flamepoints point at host-side tokenization + request serialization, not GPU.
liam: any traces/labels? which route?  
maya: route: POST /v1/stream/generate (multipart chunking). sampling trace attached: 
```
PROFILE host-side (sample=100k)
tokenize_bytes: 36%
http_writev: 22%
parse_unmarshal: 18%
kv_cache_lookup: 8%
other_syscalls: 16%
```
maya: payloads tended to be small chat turns (~200-600 bytes) but we have a burst mode that aggregates ~6k writes per request in some tails.
alex: hmm, we recently enabled the new kernel-selector heuristics in runtime that pick smaller GEMM kernels for short sequences — could that change host pacing? also there was the batching hint change that nudges more micro-batches.
nina: related note: I pushed KV cache eviction tweaks two days ago (PR #5913) that changes lookup hotness heuristics — it increased positive lookups but also added a synchronous bloom-check in the hot path. might be adding CPU and memory traffic.
ryan: can we repro locally with a microbench? try: `eng-runtime/tools/host_perf --case=stream_writev --iters=100 --payload=512` and compare before/after commits. also capture `ss -W` and a short `tcpdump -c 200 -w /tmp/w.pcap` to see write patterns.
maya: ran a quick run on canary cluster: `host_perf` shows writev latency +30us/request when payload >6k. snippet:
```
ITER 1: writev 42us
ITER 10: writev 48us
ITER 50: writev 72us (when >6kb assembled chunks)
```
maya: the trace shows more frequent `writev` syscalls (smaller chunks), which increases syscall overhead and stalls the kernel before GPU can fetch KV cache hits.
liam: sounds like two contributing factors: (1) host-side chunking changed to more aggressive micro-chunks, (2) KV bloom check is sync and on hot path. try toggling KV sync check off in local build and run the bench.
nina: agreed. I can flip the bloom-check to async in a feature-flag and run a canary. keeping the eviction heuristics as-is for now. PR draft: r/nina/async-kv-bloom-5927.
alex: I'll roll back the batching-hint commit in a local branch to see kernel-selection/batcher interplay. suspect the kernel-selector change increased tokenization CPU by adjusting quantized path selection (more CPU preproc).
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 4802467900 -> 4802468100 status: FAILED (p50 increased, auto-rollback triggered) :rotating_light:
ryan: ok plan: 1) nina feature-flag async-bloom + bench, 2) alex bisect batching-hint + bench, 3) maya collect tcpdump+perf on canary nodes and attach to issue #CORE-1428, 4) add small write coalescing at host-proxy layer as short-term fix (coalesce threshold 4k).
maya: created issue CORE-1428 with perf artifacts and linked PRs. I'll start the tcpdump/pprof upload now. :eyes:
liam: appreciate the quick triage. if async-bloom eliminates ~6-8% CPU on host path we should get p50 back. if not, coalesce patch is cheap and low-risk.
ryan: tagging eng-sre to monitor ingress writev syscalls across fleet and add a short-term metric: `host.writev.count` and `host.writev.avg_bytes` so we can alert on micro-chunk spikes.
maya: cool. I’ll post results here once we have bench numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
